ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal inverting amplifier, whose right side is the output terminal and left side is the input terminal; the output terminal returns to the input terminal through the passive feedback network below. This feedback network is composed of three series capacitors C, and when passing through these capacitors from right to left, each of the three nodes has a resistor R grounded. Mark according to the method set by the problem: the right-side amplifier output is Vout, and the three nodes with grounded resistors from right to left are respectively V1, V2, Vin, of which Vin is connected to the inverting amplifier input terminal. Reasoning: Let x = sRC, write KCL for the three nodes, and the passive feedback network transfer function can be obtained as β(s) = Vin/Vout = x^3/(x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x + 1). Let s = jω, and set u = ωRC, then β(ju) = (-j u^3)/[(1 - 6u^2) + j(5u - u^3)]. Since the amplifier is an ideal inverting amplifier, the amplifier itself provides 180° phase shift, therefore the feedback network needs to be a real negative number at the oscillation frequency. According to this expression, to make β real negative, the real part of the denominator should be zero, that is 1 - 6u^2 = 0, so u = 1/√6. Thus ωRC = 1/√6, ω = 1/(√6 RC), and the frequency f = ω/(2π) = 1/(2π√6 RC).

raw_record.question_text: For the oscillator circuit shown in the figure with an ideal inverting amplifier, what is its frequency of oscillation (in Hz)?

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology: label the right amplifier output as Vout, then moving left through the three series capacitors label the shunt-resistor nodes V1, V2, and Vin, where Vin is connected to the inverting amplifier input; each of these three nodes has a resistor R to ground. Let x=sRC and write KCL at the three shunt nodes. This gives the passive feedback transfer beta(s)=Vin/Vout = x^3/(x^3+6x^2+5x+1). Substitute s=jω and set u=ωRC, so beta(ju)=(-ju^3)/[(1-6u^2)+j(5u-u^3)]. For beta to be real negative, the real part of the denominator must vanish: 1-6u^2=0. Hence u=1/sqrt(6), so ω=1/(sqrt(6)RC) and f=ω/(2π)=1/(2π sqrt(6) R C).
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个理想反相放大器，其右侧为输出端，左侧为输入端；输出端通过下方的无源反馈网络回到输入端。该反馈网络由三个串联电容 C 组成，并且从右向左经过这些电容时，三个节点各有一个电阻 R 接地。按题设方法标记：右侧放大器输出为 Vout，从右向左三个带接地电阻的节点依次为 V1、V2、Vin，其中 Vin 接到反相放大器输入端。推理：令 x = sRC，对三个节点写 KCL，可得无源反馈网络传递函数 β(s) = Vin/Vout = x^3/(x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x + 1)。令 s = jω，并设 u = ωRC，则 β(ju) = (-j u^3)/[(1 - 6u^2) + j(5u - u^3)]。由于放大器为理想反相放大器，放大器本身提供 180° 相移，因此反馈网络在振荡频率处需为实负数。按该表达式，要使 β 为实负，分母实部应为零，即 1 - 6u^2 = 0，所以 u = 1/√6。于是 ωRC = 1/√6，ω = 1/(√6 RC)，频率 f = ω/(2π) = 1/(2π√6 RC)。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct circuit-analysis route: it derives the oscillation frequency from the actual three-section RC feedback ladder seen in the image using nodal equations and Barkhausen phase condition, rather than relying only on a memorized phase-shift oscillator formula.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as an ideal inverting amplifier whose output is fed back to its input through three identical series capacitors C, with each intermediate/input node shunted to ground by an identical resistor R. Identify the amplifier input node as the left end of the RC ladder and the amplifier output node as the right end.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the amplifier is ideal and inverting, and that the requested quantity is the oscillation frequency in Hz.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use Barkhausen criterion for an ideal inverting amplifier: the amplifier contributes 180 degrees of phase shift, so the passive feedback network must contribute another 180 degrees, i.e. its transfer ratio beta(jω)=Vin/Vout must be real and negative. Apply nodal analysis to the equal-RC ladder.
